skill.name: dittobot
skill.description: Edit, rewrite, tighten, diagnose, and adapt user-provided prose while preserving voice, facts, intent, stance, rhythm, humor, and formality.
skill.summary: Voice-faithful editing for drafts, notes, emails, posts, and other user-provided prose.
skill.author: RegionallyFamous

security_audit.summary: The main confirmed risk is the README terminal fallback that pipes a remote installer directly into bash. The installer and optional live-evaluation tooling also perform real network, filesystem, and API-key handling, while most other static hits are markdown, license text, fixtures, or bounded maintainer scripts. No prompt-injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill instructions or reference files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the curl-to-bash command and direct users to the marketplace installer, a pinned release artifact, or manual clone-and-review steps.

remediation.issue: install.sh can install code from environment-controlled repositories, refs, or archive URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Pin installation to immutable release checksums, remove broad environment overrides, or require an explicit confirmation before using custom sources.

remediation.issue: Optional live evaluation handles OPENAI_API_KEY and sends prompts to an external API.
remediation.suggestion: Keep live-eval tooling out of normal installed skill paths or add clear runtime prompts before any external request.

remediation.issue: Live-eval transcript saves can include raw model output that may contain private source text.
remediation.suggestion: Make transcript output hash-only by default, honor --save-raw-output as the only raw-output path, and update SECURITY.md after the code change.

semantic_findings.title: Environment-Controlled Remote Installer Source
semantic_findings.description: install.sh lets environment variables choose the repository, ref, or archive URL, then runs scripts/install.py from the downloaded archive. This expands the risk of the documented remote installer because an untrusted environment can redirect what code is installed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The control flow is direct: environment variables set ARCHIVE_URL and the script later executes python3 on scripts/install.py from that archive. Legitimate override use is possible, so the finding is high confidence but not treated as hidden malware intent.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Live-Eval Output Saved To Local Transcripts
semantic_findings.description: When --save-jsonl is used, scripts/live_eval.py always writes model output into the transcript. The help text and security notes warn that raw output can contain source text, so private drafts can be stored locally even without --save-raw-output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The save path is optional and chmodded, but the code unconditionally includes output in the saved record. SECURITY.md says transcript saves are hash-only by default, which conflicts with the code path.

content.user_title: Rewrite Prose in the User Voice
content.value_statement: Generic AI edits can flatten voice, add unsupported facts, or make drafts too polished. Dittobot helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code revise user-provided prose while preserving meaning, stance, and style.
actual_capabilities: Rewrites messy notes, emails, posts, captions, bios, essays, and internal documents.
Preserves facts, claims, uncertainty, names, dates, quotes, and explicit constraints.
Supports proofread, light edit, tighten, rewrite, punch up, diagnosis, options, and voice profile modes.
Uses optional fact fences for protected claims, voice markers, avoided terms, and boundaries.
Includes local regression, audit, scorecard, redaction, and live-evaluation scripts for maintainers.
limitations: Works best when the user provides source text or a clear writing sample.
Does not verify facts, legal claims, medical claims, citations, or external evidence.
Optional scripts can access files, run subprocesses, and call external APIs when invoked.
Voice profiles transfer editing taste only; they should not store private facts.

use_cases.title: Polish Work Messages
use_cases.description: Turn rough emails, chat updates, and announcements into clear prose that still sounds like the sender.

use_cases.title: Clean Public Drafts
use_cases.description: Tighten posts, essays, bios, captions, and website copy while keeping the original stance and rhythm.

use_cases.title: Maintain Voice Profiles
use_cases.description: Infer compact editing rules from samples so future rewrites preserve recurring voice choices without importing old facts.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Rewrite
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $dittobot on this. Keep my meaning and voice, but make it clearer and shorter: [paste draft]

prompt_templates.title: Tone Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare versions for a sensitive message
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $dittobot on this. Give me three versions: cleaner, warmer, and sharper. Preserve all facts: [paste draft]

prompt_templates.title: Fact-Fenced Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $dittobot on this with these fences: [[keep: 10 business days, not counsel]] [[avoid: guaranteed]] [paste draft]

prompt_templates.title: Voice Profile Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $dittobot to infer a compact voice profile from these samples, then explain when not to apply it: [paste samples]

output_examples.input: A launch note says the importer bug is fixed, but it feels too long and unclear.
output_examples.output: A shorter launch note states the bug is fixed, explains retrying failed rows, and keeps the writer calm but specific.

output_examples.input: A generic platform sentence uses broad claims and no concrete details.
output_examples.output: A modest rewrite removes inflated language and adds a brief note that the draft needs real specifics.

output_examples.input: A legally sensitive draft includes uncertainty about a notice deadline.
output_examples.output: A careful version preserves uncertainty, keeps the deadline language, and avoids turning the claim into legal advice.

best_practices: Provide the source text, audience, purpose, and hard constraints before asking for a rewrite.
Use fact fences for names, numbers, legal uncertainty, protected claims, and phrases that must survive.
Review outputs for factual accuracy before sending legal, medical, financial, academic, or public-facing text.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent missing facts, customers, metrics, citations, or legal certainty.
Do not use old voice profiles as a source of facts for a new draft.
Do not run optional install or live-evaluation scripts without reviewing filesystem and network behavior.

faq.question: Does Dittobot write from scratch?
faq.answer: It is mainly an editor. It works best from a draft, notes, or samples that establish the user voice.

faq.question: Can it preserve exact facts and claims?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to protect source facts and constraints, but users should still verify sensitive claims.

faq.question: What are fact fences?
faq.answer: Fact fences are optional markers for protected facts, required claims, voice cues, avoided terms, and boundaries.

faq.question: Does it call external services during normal use?
faq.answer: The skill instructions do not require network access. Optional live-evaluation scripts call the OpenAI API when configured.

faq.question: Can it make text less AI-sounding?
faq.answer: Yes. It removes generic filler and restores source-supported voice without adding fake errors or unsupported details.

faq.question: Is it safe for private drafts?
faq.answer: Treat private drafts as sensitive. Avoid raw transcript saves, and review optional scripts before running local tools.
